rows.check: Checked, not assumed. SCOPE FIRST: the working tree carries drift that is not this change — `git status --short` also shows .claude/settings.json, .zshrc and two .claude/sounds/*.mp3 modified, plus three untracked paths (engine-args.mjs.bak-pre-promptsfix-043a2526, mitosis.js.bak-pre-promptsfix-043a2526, .claude/skills/context7-mcp/). None of those is part of this change, I did not author or modify any of them, and all are excluded from every count below. The change proper is exactly 19 tracked paths between 6957691 and 4e32efc: four renames (mitosis-git.mjs -> git/pr.mjs R099, pr-format.mjs -> git/pr-format.mjs R100, and their two test files R099) plus 15 modifications, of which 11 are test files, 3 are docs (.claude/CLAUDE.md, rules/common/git/pull-requests.md, skills/pr/SKILL.md) and the remainder are block-destructive-bash.sh, workflows/mitosis.js and package.json. `git diff --name-only -M` over that range matched NOTHING against `sandbox|registry.json|invariant-coverage-check|receipts.yml|docs/invariants` — workflow-sandbox.mjs, the only file that constructs the realm, is absent from the path list. A CONTENT grep of the entire diff for `DONT_CONTEXTIFY|createContext|runInContext|node:vm|SandboxViolationError` returns 0 matches, so no realm, context, or global object is constructed, removed, or reconfigured anywhere in this range. The change relocates a pull-request CLI between two lib trees and rewrites path strings that name it; it introduces no vm usage and no new identifier reachable from a workflow body.

workflow-sandbox.mjs is absent from the 19-path diff, and the diff content carries 0 occurrences of SandboxViolationError or SANDBOX_VIOLATION (same grep as B1, run over the whole range). No proxy invariant, ownKeys filter, freeze, or seal is touched, so no denial path changes shape and no previously-tagged violation can degrade into an untagged host error that a workflow could catch as its own. The moved module (pr.mjs) is a CLI spawned as its own process by an agent-issued shell command; it is never compiled into or evaluated inside the sandbox realm, so relocating it cannot introduce a new throw site on any sandbox path.

Guarded-intrinsic membership is declared entirely inside workflow-sandbox.mjs, which is not among the 19 changed paths. The three suites that exercise denial membership — workflow-sandbox-policy.test.mjs, workflow-sandbox-traps.test.mjs, workflow-sandbox.test.mjs — are likewise untouched. I also confirmed they are still COLLECTED, because this change does edit the npm test globs: the package.json diff is a single replaced line that only INSERTS `.claude/lib/git/tests/*.test.mjs` as a third glob, leaving `.claude/lib/superpowers-parallel/tests/*.test.mjs` first and unmodified. Expanding that first glob in the live tree lists all four workflow-sandbox*.test.mjs files, so no guarded-intrinsic assertion silently stopped running.

VALUE_GLOBALS, ALWAYS_DENIED and ALLOWED_GLOBALS are declared in workflow-sandbox.mjs, which is not in the diff; no line of the diff mentions any of the three names. Their load-bearing proof lives in workflow-sandbox-policy.test.mjs, also untouched and — per the glob check recorded under B3 — still collected by the unmodified first npm test glob. Nothing in this change empties, shrinks, or bypasses a policy constant, and nothing changes which assertions would turn red if one were emptied.

workflow-sandbox-census.test.mjs is not in the diff, so no census row is added, removed, or reclassified and no new host-reachable identifier enters the workflow-body position. The one way this change could plausibly have threatened B5 is DE-COLLECTION rather than edit, since it modifies package.json's test globs — a census that stops running proves nothing. I checked that specifically: the package.json diff removes no glob, it inserts `.claude/lib/git/tests/*.test.mjs` between the existing superpowers-parallel glob and the hooks glob, and the superpowers-parallel glob still expands to workflow-sandbox-census.test.mjs in the live tree. The census therefore still runs and still halts on an unclassified identifier.

The real production caller is intact and I confirmed it in the live tree: mitosis-gate.mjs:1 is `import { compileWorkflow } from './workflow-sandbox.mjs';`. mitosis-gate.mjs itself is NOT in the diff — only its test file is, and only to repoint one import of pull-request constants from '../mitosis-git.mjs' to '../../git/pr.mjs'; that import names MITOSIS_GIT_* exit constants, nothing sandbox-related. Sandbox liveness therefore still rests on a genuine production caller rather than on a lint artifact. This change does extend two lint artifacts (dead-export-lint.test.mjs and mirror-guard.test.mjs) to enumerate a second lib tree, but that WIDENS what they scan and removes no obligation from any module; neither becomes a substitute for the production caller, and the workflow-sandbox.mjs MIRROR_CENSUS row is unchanged at 'standalone'.

Satisfied by this artifact. This file records a verdict for all 12 registry ids — B1-B6 and M1-M6, the whole invariant set of both tracks — and is committed to the repository rather than argued in the pull-request body; the PR body for this branch states no invariant verdict and makes no coverage claim. This entry exists because the gap was caught in review before the PR was opened: scripts/invariant-coverage-check.mjs:170-178 fails any pull_request event when no file under docs/invariants/coverage/ is added or modified between base and HEAD, and this branch touched zero files there against either candidate base. The filename follows the established branch-derived convention (refactor/relocate-pr-tool -> refactor-relocate-pr-tool.json), matching all 20 pre-existing entries.

Proven by mutation, not by reading. This change edits three gates that classify paths or identifiers, so M2 is genuinely engaged. (1) The hook's `selfwrap` regex at block-destructive-bash.sh:43 now keys on the path tail `lib/git/pr\.mjs` instead of the bare filename `mitosis-git\.mjs`; that is a strictly narrower classifier, not a count or a sampled allowlist. (2) mirror-guard's MIRROR_CENSUS rows for the two moved modules were renamed to 'git/pr.mjs' and 'git/pr-format.mjs'. (3) dead-export-lint, mirror-guard and no-self-merge-consent now enumerate BOTH lib trees. The risk is that widening the scan silently drops the halt-on-unclassifiable property for the new tree, so I tested it directly: I dropped a throwaway .claude/lib/git/zz-census-probe.mjs exporting one symbol and re-ran both scanners. mirror-guard failed with 'these lib modules have no MIRROR_CENSUS row: git/zz-census-probe.mjs' and dead-export-lint failed with 'git/zz-census-probe.mjs :: unclassifiedProbe'. Both censuses halt on the unclassifiable in the relocated tree. The probe was deleted and `git status --short` confirmed the tree clean. One pre-existing pinned count survives and I name it rather than let it pass unmentioned: PR_CREATE_SITES = 2 at gh-scope-lint.test.mjs:20, which this change consumes at three assertion sites but did not introduce and does not widen.

The red/green pair was RUN, not asserted. This increment's one behavioral change is the gate narrowing, and its acceptance test is block-destructive-bash.test.mjs:134, 'the superseded superpowers-parallel path carries no exemption, so exactly one path is canonical'. I extracted that test's command string verbatim from the test file (rather than retyping it, which would prove something else) and fed the identical hook payload to both revisions of the hook: the parent revision at 6957691 returns empty stdout — ALLOW, silent — so the test's `assert.match(r.stdout, /"permissionDecision":"deny"/)` is RED on the parent; the current revision returns permissionDecision 'deny', GREEN. The asserted symptom is the reported one: after the move exactly one path carries the wrapper exemption. Inertness is structural here — the assertion reads the hook's own decision, so reverting selfwrap to the old filename pattern restores the ALLOW and turns it red again, which is precisely what the parent-revision run demonstrates.

The condition M4 guards is genuinely present in this commit, and the exemption clause is what carries it — recorded plainly rather than glossed. This single reviewable range DOES combine a structural relocation (four renames at R099/R100, plus 15 reference updates) with a behavior change (the selfwrap classifier narrows, so the superseded path loses its exemption). M4 permits that only when a characterization test pinning the surviving behavior was written BEFORE the refactor. It was: block-destructive-bash.test.mjs is that suite and it predates this branch. I measured it on both sides instead of trusting the count — checked out the parent commit 6957691 in a throwaway worktree and ran the suite there: 84 tests, 84 pass, 0 fail. The same suite on this commit: 85 tests, 85 pass, 0 fail. Every one of the 84 pinned gate behaviors survives the relocation unchanged, and the single delta is the one new deny case that encodes the intended behavior change. The throwaway worktree was removed afterwards and `git worktree list` confirmed it gone.

Every citation was re-derived against the live tree at write time. The rename rewrote three path:line citations embedded in assertion messages in no-self-merge-consent.test.mjs — a mechanical find-and-replace preserves line numbers without ever checking them, which is exactly the copied-citation failure M5 names, so I read all three: pr.mjs:343 is `const gate = ghExecTripwire(argv, classifyGhMerge);`, pr.mjs:347 is the module's single `spawnSync(ghBin, argv, ...)`, and tests/pr.test.mjs:969 is `test('the wrapper module contains no merge or approval subcommand anywhere in its source', ...)`. All three resolve to exactly what the surrounding message claims about them, so the rename did not shift the cited lines. Every path:line appearing in this coverage file was likewise read in the live tree today, including block-destructive-bash.sh:43, block-destructive-bash.test.mjs:134, gh-scope-lint.test.mjs:20, mitosis-gate.mjs:1 and invariant-coverage-check.mjs:170-178.

The deployed artifacts were inspected, not assumed — and one assumption made during review turned out to be wrong, which is why this was checked. The artifact that enforces PR centralization is .claude/hooks/block-destructive-bash.sh; its deployed instance at ~/.claude/hooks/block-destructive-bash.sh is a SYMLINK whose target `ls -la` resolves to the committed file in this repository, so the enforcing artifact IS the committed source at this SHA, there is no separate build to refresh, and a hand-patched deployed copy is structurally impossible for the gate. The relocated tool deploys differently and an earlier review described it as symlinked; it is not. ~/.claude/lib/git/pr.mjs and ~/.claude/lib/git/pr-format.mjs are regular files — copies — so I diffed both against the committed copies and both are byte-identical, and I confirmed the three cross-tree imports the moved tool makes resolve at the deployed location (gh-merge-shim.mjs, checkpoint.mjs and merge-watch.mjs all present under ~/.claude/lib/superpowers-parallel/). Copy-rather-than-symlink is the pre-existing convention for the entire ~/.claude/lib tree, including the superpowers-parallel directory this tool came from; this change neither introduces nor worsens it, and the deployed guard reproduces the committed one exactly.
